subject: Residency fallback & log retention follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Long <sarah.long@avahealth.com>, security@avahealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Residenc[y] fallback & log retention follow-up

Hi Sarah / Ava security team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can finalize the residency constraints for the pilot.

Key items we captured on our side:
- Primary region requirement: US-east for production workloads; EU for patient-facing EU customers; APAC for Singapore/JP pilots.
- Failover behavior: you said cross-region fallback is allowed for short windows during outage, provided data does not persist outside the primary region beyond the recovery window.
- Logs & telemetry: you require audit logs for 12 months, but PII must be redacted from operational logs and any exported backups.

Open questions we promised to get clarified:
1) Exact RPO/RTO targets for cross-region failover (we noted 15m RTO / 1h RPO as a starting point — confirm?)
2) Does snapshot backup egress to a different region count as a residency violation if the copy is encrypted and access-controlled?
3) Which fields in logs are considered PII for Ava? (examples: user_id, email, IP, full content)
4) Is a hashed identifier acceptable for analytics traces or do you require full redaction?

Next steps from Redwood: we can prepare a short matrix mapping feature -> default policy -> customer override (pin to region / allow transient failover / no-eject backups). I'll attach a first-draft matrix after internal review.

Please reply with short answers to Q1–Q4 when you have a moment; that will let us size Dedicated capacity and confirm whether Private (VPC) is a hard requirement.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up if easier.

Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sarah Long <sarah.long@avahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residenc[y] fallback & log retention follow-up

Thanks Marcus — good recap. Quick answers inline: 

Q1) RPO/RTO: For our initial launch we need RTO <= 30 minutes and RPO <= 2 hours. We can consider relaxed RPO for non-critical analytics buckets.

Q2) Backup egress: Any automated snapshot or backup that physically leaves the designated legal region is a violation for patient data. Encrypted copies that leave for DR are acceptable only if the data is first tokenized/approved by our security team and a legal exception is in place.

Q3) PII fields: a short list — full name, email, phone number, government IDs, DOB, full address, unredacted SSNs. We also consider unredacted message content that includes identifiers as PII.

Q4) Hashed identifiers: hashed IDs are acceptable for analytics as long as the hashing is irreversible within our threat model and salts are managed by Ava (we prefer customer-managed salts).

Also a couple of follow-ups from our security engineering team:
- Can Redwood provide an exportable audit log schema and explain how you ensure PII is not accidentally logged in model inputs/outputs?
- What options exist for log sampling vs full logging (we want full audit trails for admin events, sampled for debug traces)?

CCing security@avahealth.com per request. Happy to set a 30-min follow-up Friday if useful.

— Sarah
Sarah Long
Director of Product Security | Ava Health
sarah.long@avahealth.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Long <sarah.long@avahealth.com>, security@avahealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residenc[y] fallback & log retention follow-up

Sarah — really helpful, thanks. Notes and asks for confirmation below, and attaching the first-draft matrix.

Confirmed (per your answers):
- Launch RTO <= 30m, RPO <= 2h for critical patient pipelines.
- No automated snapshot backups permitted to cross legal regions for patient data without a documented legal exception and tokenization.
- PII list acknowledged — we'll mark those fields for mandatory redaction in any operational logs.
- Hashed IDs acceptable if customer-managed salts are used.

Follow-up asks (for security team):
- Please confirm whether customer-managed KMS/HSM is required for encryption-at-rest, or if our KMS with a signed-access attestation is acceptable for the pilot.
- For model output retention: can Redwood keep model outputs for 7 days for debugging if outputs are encrypted-at-rest and logs are PII-redacted?

Attachment: ava_residency_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix maps policy rows: workload type, default region, allowed transient failover, backup egress permitted, log retention, notes).

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) We finalize this matrix with your security team answers and produce a pilot scoping doc.
2) Solutions engineering (Monica & Aditya) will produce an environment diagram showing where backups and caches live and whether they replicate cross-region.
3) If needed, schedule a 30-min technical follow-up Friday to lock KMS/HSM approach.

If that sequence looks good I will: (A) update the matrix per any edits and (B) have Monica prepare a short notes doc on how our KV cache and prefix caching behaves during failover windows.

Thanks — attaching matrix now.

Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: SE scope & notes for Ava Health residency pilot

Monica / Aditya — moving this to internal thread to scope SE work now that Sarah responded. Key asks to cover in the technical note: 
- Show diagram of primary region (us-east) and explicit transient failover mechanics (how KV cache is invalidated, whether prefix caching persists across failover, and where warmed copies live).
- Define where backups are stored for each workload and confirm that patient-data snapshots never leave primary legal region unless tokenized and under legal exception.
- Provide an audit-log schema: which fields we collect by default, which fields are redacted, and how to export logs for Ava's retention (12 months).
- KMS options: outline steps for customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed KMS with attestation; include required changes to onboarding checklist.
- RTO/RPO feasibility: confirm we can meet RTO 30m / RPO 2h for the pilot on Dedicated capacity; call out any caveats (warm standby, burst capacity needs).

Can you draft a 1-page SE note + a short diagram by EOD Monday so I can share back with Sarah and legal? I'll include the matrix we sent as an attachment.

Thanks — Marcus
